extracted.intended_audience: readers, students, and writers studying modern Chinese literature and Lu Xun's literary style
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting the stylistic, thematic, and formal qualities of Lu Xun's writing (how he wrote and why his work was valued), to inform literary analysis or creative-writing practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing in both vernacular and literary Chinese
rubrics_metrics.description: Lu Xun "wrote in both vernacular and literary Chinese" and pioneered publishing in vernacular (e.g., Diary of a Madman is cited as the first novel in vernacular Chinese).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using vernacular makes work accessible and politically modernizing (New Culture Movement); switching between registers can be a deliberate stylistic and audience choice. Example: Diary of a Madman launched his prominence because of its vernacular form. Anti-pattern: writing only in overly erudite literary Chinese limits popular reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharp, satirical style; mastery of irony
rubrics_metrics.description: He was "known for his sharp, satirical style" and is repeatedly described as a "master of irony and satire" (e.g., The True Story of Ah Q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satire and irony are key tools for social critique—use veiled ridicule, caricature, and ironic narration to expose cultural follies. Example works: "The True Story of Ah Q" and "Diary of a Madman". Anti-pattern: satire without moral or political insight can read merely cynical or mean-spirited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical reflections on Chinese history and culture / anti-traditionalism
rubrics_metrics.description: His writing offers "critical reflections on Chinese history and culture" and was praised for its "anti-traditionalism."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly interrogate cultural norms and historical practices; make critique integral to character and plot. Lu Xun's notoriety derived partly from attacking traditional values. Anti-pattern: superficial denunciation that lacks concrete depiction of cultural consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesis of Chinese and foreign conventions and forms
rubrics_metrics.description: His fiction was praised for its "synthesis of Chinese and foreign conventions and ideas" and he wrote "using both traditional Chinese conventions and 19th century European literary forms."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blend indigenous narrative techniques with imported forms (e.g., realist/psychological modes) to innovate. Example: combining Chinese vernacular storytelling with European narrative structures. Anti-pattern: mimicry of foreign forms without integrating local idioms or concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fresh, direct language; clarity and lucidity
rubrics_metrics.description: His work—especially 'peasant dirt literature'—is noted for "language is fresh and direct" and a "clear lucid style."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor immediacy, simple diction, and transparent phrasing to convey social realism and emotional truth. This clarity aided influence across generations. Anti-pattern: overwriting or ornate style that obscures social critique or character voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on peasants and everyday people ('peasant dirt literature')
rubrics_metrics.description: Lu Xun's greatest works "exemplify this style of 'peasant dirt literature'... The language is fresh and direct. The subjects are country peasants."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Center marginalized, rural, or working-class characters to reveal broader social conditions; use concrete local detail. This grounds social critique in lived experience. Anti-pattern: using peasants only as symbols rather than fleshed characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incisive social commentary; writing as a 'literary physician'
rubrics_metrics.description: His essays are "often incisive in his societal commentary," and he described becoming a "literary physician to what he perceived to be China's spiritual problems."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write with an explicit diagnostic intent—identify social ills and make writing a vehicle for awakening or reform. Use essays and fiction to diagnose and dramatize cultural maladies. Anti-pattern: aestheticism detached from urgent social purpose when aim is civic critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing sympathetic engagement and ironic detachment
rubrics_metrics.description: His style is said to convey both "sympathetic engagement" and "ironic detachment" at different moments, and he "frequently treads a fine line between criticizing the follies of his characters and sympathizing with those very follies."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine compassion for characters with critical distance: portray human frailty empathetically while holding broader social forces to account. Anti-pattern: unrelieved pity that removes critique or relentless irony that erases sympathy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skillful narration and storytelling technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Works were praised for "skillful narration" (e.g., early stories that gained prominence for their narration and anti-traditionalism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ narrative strategies—point of view, voice, pacing, and framing—to shape irony, revelation, and moral perspective. Example: using unreliable narration to produce satirical effects. Anti-pattern: flat or inconsistent narrative voice that undermines intended irony or empathy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versatility across genres and media
rubrics_metrics.description: Lu Xun "contributed significantly to nearly every modern literary medium"—stories, prose poems, essays, poetry, translation, criticism—and was a leader of the Woodcut Movement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate facility across forms (fiction, essays, translation, visual media) to broaden influence and experiment with modes of social engagement. Anti-pattern: rigid adherence to a single form when the work’s purpose could benefit from cross-media expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation and acute literary criticism as part of craft
rubrics_metrics.description: His translations were important in introducing foreign literature, and his "literary criticisms remain acute and persuasively argued."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use translation and critical writing both to import useful modes and to refine one's own practice; rigorous criticism can clarify artistic aims. Anti-pattern: careless translation that flattens source voice or criticism that is polemical without analytic depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of visual/print media to promote social change (woodcut movement)
rubrics_metrics.description: He was a leader of the Woodcut Movement and "envisioned [woodcut] as a medium to promote social change and 'an alternative socialist road to art.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider non-literary media (printmaking, illustration) as allied forms for political messaging and mass circulation. Anti-pattern: treating visual media merely decoratively rather than as a programmatic social tool.
